name: Blackstone Private Credit Fund
type: Non-traded BDC, perpetual, for individual investors
liquidity: Quarterly buybacks, capped at 5% of shares
dek: The flagship of private credit's push to individual investors, and this year the test of how a semi-liquid fund behaves when many holders want out at once.

timeline.what: Launches at $25 a share, giving wealthy individuals access to Blackstone's direct lending through a fund with monthly subscriptions and quarterly repurchases.
Repurchase requests hit a then-record of about 7.9% of shares (reported as $3.7bn to $3.8bn). All requests are met, with Blackstone and its employees putting in about $400m.
Requests rise to about 10% of shares ($4.5bn). For the first time the fund holds to its 5% cap, paying roughly half of what was asked and leaving a backlog of about $2.3bn.
Requests stay near 10% (about $4.3bn). The fund again fills 5%, paying about $2.13bn; after $750m of new subscriptions, net outflows are about 3% of NAV.
Reports an 8.9% annualized net return since inception (Class I shares), and 10% EBITDA growth across its borrowers over the last twelve months.

why: It is the benchmark for semi-liquid private credit: how BCRED handles redemptions sets expectations for every similar fund.
The 5% cap is the design working as intended, but it means investors can wait several quarters to get all their money out.
Its returns and borrower data are one of the few regular, public windows into large-scale direct lending.
